target_customer: Small and growing businesses and e-commerce brands that need custom branded shipping packaging in small quantities
problem: Ordering custom packaging was slow and required large minimum orders, so startups struggled to prototype and ship branded boxes.
business_model: E-commerce sales of custom packaging with design tools, starting at $1 per box for orders of 10 to 10,000 units

founders.name: Nick Carson
founders.background_notes: TechCrunch March 2015: handled packaging for buyback programs at iCracked.

founders.name: Phillip Akhzar
founders.background_notes: YC page links Arka.com as his later company.

exit.reason: Not public. PitchBook lists it as out of business and CB Insights as dead; no announcement or post-mortem found.

technical_complexity.rationale: A web store with box mockup tools on top of outsourced print and corrugated manufacturing.

defensibility.rationale: Packaging suppliers and similar online players (Packlane and Packhelp, both listed as founded in 2015 on undated profiles) could copy the model easily.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent response was found; the company ended operations at an undated point.

market_need_then: TechCrunch March 2015 reported the founders secured $40,000 in letters of intent after six months of testing and orders for 800,000 units, with clients such as Level Frames and Sirum.

identity.voice_and_tone: Startup friendly, pitched as Teespring for packaging with a 10 boxes for $10 first order offer

branding.community_and_virality: Covered by TechCrunch and TrendHunter in 2015. No community found.

brand_strength.rationale: Early press about the offer, but no evidence of a lasting brand.

outcome_analysis: Pakible left YC in Winter 2015 with reported letters of intent and 800,000 units of orders for custom packaging, then reportedly raised a seed in January 2016. It later went out of business, but no date or cause is public. The cause is not public, so failure factors stay empty.
notes: pakible.com returned HTTP 503 from this session.
